lessons.title: What you control
lessons.idea: Split every worry into two lists: what you control (your actions, words, effort) and what you don't (other people, the past, outcomes). Spend energy only on the first list.
lessons.action: Write today's top worry and circle the one part you control.

quiz.q: Which of these is within your control?
options: Your reply to a rude message

lessons.title: The morning review
lessons.idea: Marcus Aurelius began each day expecting difficult people, so they didn't shock him. Preparing for friction keeps you calm when it comes.
lessons.action: Before work, name one hard moment you might face and how you'll respond.

quiz.q: Why prepare for difficult people in the morning?
options: So their behaviour doesn't throw you off

lessons.title: Pause before reacting
lessons.idea: Between what happens and how you react there is a gap. Stoics train to widen it: breathe, judge the facts, then act.
lessons.action: Next time you feel anger, count to ten before you speak.

quiz.q: What do Stoics train to widen?
options: The gap between event and reaction

lessons.title: Love your fate
lessons.idea: Amor fati means accepting what happens and using it as material for growth, not wishing it away.
lessons.action: Pick one setback this month. Write one thing it taught you.

options: Loving and using what happens to you

lessons.title: Your inner citadel
lessons.idea: Your mind is a fortress no one can enter without your permission. Insults only hurt if you agree with them.
lessons.action: When criticised today, ask: is it true? If yes, learn. If not, let it go.

quiz.q: According to the Inner Citadel idea, insults hurt when…

lessons.title: Hidden lessons in hardship
lessons.idea: Stoics practised discomfort on purpose, cold baths, simple meals, so that hard times felt familiar instead of frightening.
lessons.action: Choose one small voluntary discomfort today: skip a treat or take the stairs.

options: So real hardship feels less frightening

lessons.title: Daily discipline
lessons.idea: Discipline is not a mood; it's a system. Small daily routines beat big bursts of motivation.
lessons.action: Set one 10-minute habit and do it at the same time every day this week.

lessons.title: Stoic love
lessons.idea: Loving well means wanting the good of the other person, not controlling them. Give care freely; don't make it a trade.
lessons.action: Do one kind act for someone close today without expecting anything back.

options: Wanting their good without making it a trade

lessons.title: The evening review
lessons.idea: Seneca reviewed each day at night: what did I do well, where did I fall short, what will I do better tomorrow?
lessons.action: Tonight, answer those three questions in two minutes.

options: What I did well, where I fell short, what I'll improve

lessons.title: Memento mori
lessons.idea: Remembering life is short is not morbid; it sharpens priorities and stops you wasting days on small things.
lessons.action: Ask: if I had one year left, what would I stop doing? Stop one thing this week.

lessons.title: Lead like you mean it
lessons.idea: People follow leaders who show up consistently. Your behaviour on ordinary days builds more trust than speeches on big days.
lessons.action: Keep one small promise to your team today, on time.

lessons.title: Influence over authority
lessons.idea: Authority makes people comply; influence makes them commit. Influence comes from listening, credibility and helping others win.
lessons.action: Ask one team member what's blocking them and remove one obstacle.

lessons.title: The empathic edge
lessons.idea: Empathy is a performance tool: when people feel understood, they share problems early, before they become crises.
lessons.action: In your next one-on-one, listen for two minutes before giving any advice.

quiz.q: Why is empathy a performance tool?

lessons.title: From boss to beacon
lessons.idea: A boss checks work; a beacon shows the way. Set the direction clearly and people can find their own path to it.
lessons.action: Write your team's goal for this month in one sentence and share it.

lessons.title: The human side
lessons.idea: In the age of AI, trust and emotional intelligence become a leader's edge, because they're the hardest things to automate.
lessons.action: Thank one person specifically: name what they did and why it mattered.

quiz.q: What becomes a leader's edge in the age of AI?

lessons.title: People over process
lessons.idea: Processes should serve people, not the other way round. When a rule blocks good work, fix the rule.
lessons.action: Find one rule or step that slows your team for no reason and question it.

quiz.q: When a rule blocks good work, you should…

lessons.title: Delegate decisions, not tasks
lessons.idea: Give people ownership of decisions within clear limits, such as 'anything under 5 million is your call', and they'll move faster than if every approval waits for you.
lessons.action: Set one decision limit for someone on your team this week.

lessons.title: The one true leader
lessons.idea: The leader you are under pressure is the real one. Calm, fair behaviour in a crisis earns lasting loyalty.
lessons.action: Recall your last crisis: what would you do differently? Write it down.

lessons.title: Feedback that lands
lessons.idea: Good feedback is specific, timely and about behaviour, not personality: 'the report was late' not 'you're lazy'.
lessons.action: Give one piece of specific, kind feedback today.

lessons.title: The art of growth
lessons.idea: Great leaders grow people who can replace them. Your success is measured by how strong your team is without you.
lessons.action: Teach someone one task you usually do yourself.

quiz.q: A leader's success is measured by…
options: How strong the team is without them

lessons.title: Your human operating system
lessons.idea: Your habits are like code: they run automatically. Change the code and you change the results.
lessons.action: List three habits that run your day. Mark one to rewrite.

lessons.title: The focus code
lessons.idea: Focus is a resource that runs out. Protect your best hours for your hardest work and push meetings and messages later.
lessons.action: Block 60 minutes tomorrow for one important task, phone away.

quiz.q: When should you do your hardest work?

lessons.title: Human algorithms
lessons.idea: Simple rules decide faster than moods: 'if a task takes under 2 minutes, do it now.'
lessons.action: Write one 'if X, then Y' rule for a decision you keep repeating.

lessons.title: Calm under fire
lessons.idea: When pressure hits, slow your breathing first. A calm body lets the thinking brain work.
lessons.action: Practise 4-7-8 breathing once today: in 4, hold 7, out 8.

quiz.q: What should you do first under pressure?

lessons.title: Inner algorithms
lessons.idea: Your self-talk is a program. Replace 'I can't' with 'not yet' and your brain keeps searching for solutions.
lessons.action: Catch one negative thought today and rewrite it.

options: Keeps your brain searching for solutions

lessons.title: The human bottleneck
lessons.idea: In most teams the slowest step is a person waiting for a decision, often the leader. Remove yourself as the bottleneck.
lessons.action: Find one thing that waits on you and hand it over.

quiz.q: In most teams, the slowest step is often…
options: A person waiting for a decision

lessons.title: The systems leader
lessons.idea: Don't fix the same problem twice. When something goes wrong, fix the system that allowed it.
lessons.action: Pick a repeated problem and write one change that stops it recurring.

lessons.title: The calm team
lessons.idea: Calm spreads. A leader's tone sets the team's stress level, so lower your voice when things heat up.
lessons.action: In your next tense meeting, speak slower and softer than usual.

lessons.title: Built for volatility
lessons.idea: You can't predict every shock, but you can build buffers: savings, backups, and people trained to cover for each other.
lessons.action: Name one buffer you'll build this month: money, a backup person or a process.

quiz.q: How do you prepare for shocks you can't predict?

lessons.title: Rest is a strategy
lessons.idea: Sleep and breaks are not laziness; they restore focus. Tired brains make costly decisions.
lessons.action: Set a fixed bedtime for this week and keep it.

options: It restores focus and decision quality
